Review branch `fix/tui-resize-repaint` in /home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek (uncommitted, diff against `main`). This closes #46 and it is squarely in your remit — it changes how the full-screen interface behaves under the player's hands.

What changed in `tui.c`:
1. `tui_getch()` (the paging pause) — on `KEY_RESIZE` it now calls `tui_refresh_panels()` and waits again, instead of silently swallowing the resize and leaving the old screen until the player pressed a key. Safe there because curses reports the resize *by returning from* `wgetch`, so nothing is reading the screen at that moment.
2. `tui_readline()` — `wgetnstr` is replaced by a hand-rolled reader that takes one keystroke at a time: printable ASCII, backspace, Enter, Ctrl-D, and `KEY_RESIZE` handled between keystrokes. This is what lets a resize be redrawn mid-prompt, and it keeps the partially typed line, which `wgetnstr` discarded. Ctrl-D on an empty line now ends the session on its own keystroke instead of needing an Enter after it.

`tests/tui.sh` gains three sections: resize during a pause, resize while an answer is half typed, and Ctrl-D.

Please be hard on this from the player's side — a hand-rolled line editor is exactly where a terminal game gets subtly worse:
- **Typing feel.** Does the prompt behave as a player expects at 80x24 and 72x24? Backspace at the start of a line, backspace past the prompt (it must not eat the prompt or the panel border), a very long answer that wraps or hits the buffer limit, fast typing, holding a key down.
- **Keys that are no longer accepted.** The reader takes printable ASCII only, so arrow keys, Home/End, Delete, Tab and pasted text with control characters are now ignored rather than inserted. Is any of that a regression a player would feel? Pasting a command is the case I am least sure about.
- **The resize behaviour itself** at both sizes, during a pause and mid-typing, including shrinking (not just growing) and a resize below the 72x24 minimum.
- **Ctrl-C, Ctrl-U, Ctrl-W** and anything else a terminal user might reflexively press at a prompt.
- Whether the paging pause still needs exactly one keystroke, and whether a resize can still page away unread text.

input.message:
All three should-fixes addressed, plus the comment nit. Please re-review — particularly the shrink case, which is the one I want you to try to break again.

**1 (shrinking loses the prompt and unread text).** You were right and this was the serious one. `wresize` keeps the top of the window, so the rows it drops are exactly where the newest text and the prompt live. `make_windows()` now scrolls the difference away *before* resizing when the message window is losing height, so the oldest rows go instead of the newest:

```c
int oldh = getmaxy(wmsg);
if (msgh < oldh)
    wscrl(wmsg, oldh - msgh);
```

Verified at 100x30 → 72x24 during a `help move` pause: before the fix all four bottom lines including `[HIT SPACE BAR TO CONTINUE]` were gone; now the prompt and the three lines of help above it survive, and one Space still advances exactly one page rather than skipping the text that used to be discarded.

**2 (backspace across a wrapped answer).** Fixed — `erase_one()` now steps to the end of the row above when the cursor is at column 0, instead of returning and letting the buffer and the screen disagree. The `len > 0` guard is what keeps it off the prompt, since it can never erase more characters than were typed.

**3 (Ctrl-U).** Restored — it erases the whole line, screen and buffer together, with a comment saying it was the one piece of line editing `wgetnstr` had that this reader would otherwise have dropped.

**7 (the stale comment).** `tui_getch`'s note no longer says "the line read below" — `tui_readline` is above it, and it is no longer something you cannot repaint under.

I also took the README suggestion: one sentence saying the display follows the terminal, including mid-answer.

**Something you should know before you re-test.** While checking the shrink fix I hit `COMMAND> sc` where `srsc` had been typed, and chased it as a possible new bug. It reproduces identically on a pre-fix binary built from `main`, and the cause is mundane: `help move` has more pages than the four Spaces I was sending, so the `s` and `r` answered the remaining pause prompts before the game reached the command prompt. Not a regression, and not timing — a three-second settle makes no difference. Flagging it so you do not spend the time I did.

**6 (sub-minimum garbling)** is filed as #78 rather than fixed here: it predates the change, and deciding between "say the terminal is too small" and "genuinely clip" is a design call that deserves its own slice. The issue records that #46 made it more visible rather than caused it.

**4 and 5** (ignored keys; the silent buffer cap) will be called out in the commit as deliberate, as you asked.

The three new test sections still pass on the fixed build and all five of their assertions still fail against a pre-fix binary. I have not yet added a shrink case to the tests — tell me whether you want it in `tui.sh` given the pause section already resizes, or whether the growth case plus the manual shrink evidence is enough.

input.message:
Your finding 1 was deeper than either of us thought, and my first two fixes for it were wrong. The state has changed enough since my last message that I would ignore that one and re-test from scratch — especially the shrink.

**What was actually happening.** Curses clips the message window when *it* processes the resize, and it does that before handing the game `KEY_RESIZE`. So the bottom rows — the newest text, the prompt — are gone before any of the game's code runs. I proved it by instrumenting a scratch build: at the moment the game is told, `getmaxy(wmsg)` already reads 24 where the window had been 27.

That killed two attempts:
- scrolling the height difference away before resizing — the content sits at the *top* until the conversation has filled the window, so this threw away everything and left a blank panel (100x30 → 72x24 looked fixed, 120x40 → 72x24 went blank);
- doing the same before `resize_term` via a `TIOCGWINSZ` ioctl — too late as well, for the reason above.

**What works.** `tui.c` now keeps `curline`, the text since the last newline, updated in `tui_puts`/`tui_puts_slow`. After a resize the repaint reads the row the cursor is on and reprints that line only if the clip took it — so the prompt comes back on a shrink and is not duplicated on a growth. `tui_readline` re-echoes its buffer after that, so the answer follows the prompt back onto the screen.

Measured across five directions, all showing the prompt exactly once and the page text intact: 80x24→120x40, 100x30→72x24, 120x40→72x24, 80x24→72x24, 72x24→100x30. The 120x40→72x24 case is the one that was blank.

**Your other findings:** backspace across a wrapped line steps to the row above now; Ctrl-U restored; the stale `tui_getch` comment fixed; README sentence added.

**Tests.** `tui.sh` has a shrink block as you asked (120x40 → 72x24, the case that failed). Seven of its eight new assertions fail against a pre-fix binary and all pass against this one. The eighth — "shrinking paged away unread text" — passes pre-fix too, because the clip took the prompt and left that text; I kept it as a property worth holding and said so in the comment rather than let it look like evidence.

Please re-run your typing-feel checks as well as the resize ones: `curline` is written on every output line now, and the reader re-echoes into the window after a repaint, so I would like both paths re-tested rather than assumed. #78 is filed for the sub-minimum garbling.

input.message:
All three reproduced defects fixed, and one of them had a cause worth telling you. Please re-test.

**1 (answer echoed twice).** `restore_curline()` now reports whether it actually wrote the line out again, and `tui_readline` re-echoes its buffer only in that case. Measured across all six of your directions with `srsc` pending — 80x24→120x40, 80x24→100x30, 72x24→100x30, 80x24→72x24, 100x30→72x24, 120x40→72x24 — every one now reads ` COMMAND> srsc` exactly once. Your point about the test pattern was right and it is now anchored (`'COMMAND> *srsc *$'`), with a comment saying an unanchored one matched `srscsrsc` happily while the bug was live.

**2 (setup questions duplicated).** Your diagnosis of the mechanism was right but the root cause was mine, one level down: the reader writes the newline on Enter straight to the window, bypassing `note_out`, so `curline` never ended and grew across prompts. The remembered line became "Would you like a regular, tournament, or frozen game?Type in tournament number-", which exists on no single row, so the search failed and appended a copy. The reader now tells `note_out` about that newline. Both blockers fixed, and your suggested fix for the first was better than what I had — it deleted a flag rather than adding a condition. Please try to break it again.

**1 (cursor in front of the answer).** Taken exactly as you proposed: `restore_curline()` always leaves the cursor at the end of `curline`, and `tui_readline` re-echoes `buf` unconditionally from there. Where the answer survived on screen it writes the same characters over themselves; where it did not it supplies them. `line_restored` is gone. Measured by typing `srsc`, resizing, then typing `an`: all six directions now read ` COMMAND> srscan` — 80x24→120x40, 80x24→100x30, 72x24→100x30, 80x24→72x24, 100x30→72x24, 120x40→72x24.

**2 (matching an older prompt).** A match now counts only as the last thing on the screen: nothing but blanks after it on its row, and nothing but blank rows below. ` COMMAND> damages` fails both and is treated as missing, so the line is reprinted at the bottom. Measured with `status`, `damages`, `rest 1` behind it, then typing `ch` after the shrink — 100x30→100x24, 80x30→80x24, 100x30→72x24, 120x40→72x24 all put it on a fresh prompt at the bottom.

**Tests.** Both of your suggested assertions are in: the line after the answer is finished (`'COMMAND> *srscan *$'`), and a new block that runs two commands before shrinking and asserts the last non-blank line is the live prompt with nothing after it, then finishes the command and checks it ran. Nine assertions now fail against a pre-fix binary and all pass against this one.

**Re-verified after the change, since these came from earlier rounds:** the doubled answer (once in all six), duplicated setup questions (one copy on growth), the chopped line (`current warp factor (see "WARP FACTOR").` whole), and the pause across three directions with one prompt and the page text intact.

**On the README (your nit 3):** with finding 2 fixed the sentence "a terminal that gets smaller keeps the question and the answer" should now be true — please confirm that, since you are better placed to judge it than I am.

Full `ctest` is rerunning in both build types. If this round is clean I will take it to the verifier and code-review; if it is not, I would rather hear it now than after it lands.

`tui.c` now keeps `pending_answer`, set by `tui_readline` around its `tui_refresh_panels()` call and NULL at a pause. `restore_curline()` builds the line it expects to see — `curline` plus whatever the reader has echoed — and looks for *that* on the last non-blank row, requiring blanks only after the pair. A surviving prompt-plus-answer is recognised and nothing is drawn; the cursor still goes to the end of `curline`, so the unconditional re-echo writes the same characters over themselves. The comment states the invariant in your words: the bottom of the conversation is the game's unfinished line and the player's unfinished answer, and the restore compares against both.

Measured, with `srsc` pending:
- one prompt in all six directions — 80x24→120x40, 80x24→100x30, 72x24→100x30, 80x24→72x24, 100x30→72x24, 120x40→72x24, each still reading ` COMMAND> srsc`;
- the twelve-step widen drag that stood up eight copies: **one** prompt, and finishing with `an` runs `srscan`;
- six alternating resizes: **one** prompt.

Your point about the tests was right and the count assertion is in: after the resize with an answer pending, `screen | grep -c 'COMMAND>'` must be 1, with a comment saying the line-shape check cannot see a duplicate because the last copy looks perfectly correct. Nine assertions fail against a pre-fix binary, all pass here, and `ctest` is rerunning in both build types.

Two things I would like you to be unkind about, since this is the fourth round and each has moved the failure somewhere new:
1. The setup conversation with an answer pending, in both directions — that is where the pending-answer path and the not-yet-full window overlap, and both have surprised me before.
2. Anything where `curline` and the echoed answer are not adjacent on one row: an answer long enough to wrap, and a prompt long enough to wrap on its own at 72 columns.

Four of your five wrap cases are fixed; the fifth I have left and documented, and I would like you to say whether you accept that.

**What I did.** Your multi-row join did not work on its own: a width change makes curses re-lay the rows and pad them, so the joined text has blanks in the middle and never matches. What does work is not searching at all when there is nothing to find — a terminal that only grew clipped nothing, so `sync_size` now calls the restore only when `LINES` or `COLS` went *down*. That closes 72x24→100x30 with `emeritus maybe` pending, 80x24→100x30 with 75 characters typed, 80x30→110x30, and the twelve-step widen drag, which is now one prompt where it was four.

That change also broke the re-echo and the suite caught it: skipping the restore leaves the cursor after the answer, so re-echoing doubled it. The re-echo is now conditional on the restore having actually repositioned the cursor (`cursor_at_prompt`), which is the honest version of the flag I deleted two rounds ago — it means "the cursor is at the end of the prompt", not "the line was reprinted".

**The one I left: a width shrink that clips a wrapped pair** (110x30 → 80x30 with 75 characters typed). The line genuinely no longer fits, curses truncates it, and the restore writes a fresh copy below the stump. Measured: the live prompt is the last thing on screen, holds the whole answer re-wrapped at the new width, and finishing it runs the command. #46 asks for the answer to be preserved or clearly restarted rather than half eaten, and this is the second of those, so I have documented it in `restore_curline` rather than chase it further. This is the fifth round and the last two findings have both come from the same place — the restore trying to work out what is on screen. If you see a sixth of that shape, say so plainly and I will stop trying to detect it and simply reprint on every clip, duplicates and all.

input.prompt:
Code-review branch `fix/tui-resize-repaint` in /home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek: the diff against `main` plus all staged, unstaged and untracked files. Three files: `tui.c`, `tests/tui.sh`, `README.md`.

Closes #46 (a resize during a prompt or pause left the display stale until the player pressed a key). This has been through five rounds of `ui-review` and one `verifier` pass; both found real defects each round, so please assume there is a sixth and look for it.

What the change does in `tui.c`:
- `tui_getch` repaints on `KEY_RESIZE` instead of swallowing it. Safe because curses reports the resize *by returning from* `wgetch`.
- `wgetnstr` is replaced by a hand-rolled reader: printable ASCII, backspace (with `erase_one` stepping to the row above at a wrap), Ctrl-U, Ctrl-D (now ends the session on its own keystroke), Enter, and `KEY_RESIZE` handled between keystrokes.
- The hard part: **curses clips the message window when it processes the resize, before the game is told**, so a shrink destroys the prompt and the typed answer before any of this code runs. So `tui.c` keeps `curline` (the game's line since the last newline, recorded in `tui_puts`/`tui_puts_slow`) and `pending_answer` (what the reader has echoed), and `restore_curline()` puts them back when they were clipped.
- `sync_size` skips the restore entirely when the terminal only grew (nothing can have been clipped), and passes the old message width when the width shrank so the stump's height is computed arithmetically rather than searched for.
- `cursor_at_prompt` tells the reader whether the repaint repositioned the cursor, so the re-echo does not double the answer.

Please review as an expert in C, ncurses and POSIX shell. Specifically:
- **The state machine.** `curline`, `curlen`, `pending_answer`, `cursor_at_prompt` are four pieces of static state maintained across three functions. Is there a path that leaves them inconsistent — an early return, a second game (`tui_gameover`/`tui_clearmsg`), a resize during `tui_puts_slow`, or a game line longer than `curline`'s 255 bytes?
- **`restore_curline`.** The row arithmetic (`start`, `i / width`, `i % width`, `maxy - rows`), the `strncat` bound, and whether `wclrtoeol` over the bottom rows can erase something that should have survived.
- **The reader's contract**: `buf`/`buflen` from `readinput()`, the `"\n"` append, the `room = buflen-2` guard.
- Whether any of this can affect **plain mode** (it must not) or the non-resize TUI path.
- The tests: are the new assertions in `tests/tui.sh` meaningful, and does anything there pass against a broken build?
Give an explicit approve / request-changes verdict.

input.message:
All five taken, and finding 1 was a genuine sixth defect of the shape the earlier rounds kept producing. Please re-review.

**1 (anchored to the bottom rather than to the line).** Fixed as you suggested: the scan that finds the last non-blank row now keeps it in `last`, and the rewrite anchors there — `r = (last >= 0 ? last : maxy - 1) - rows + 1`. When the height shrank, `last` is the bottom row and the behaviour is unchanged; when it did not, the stump is erased in place and there is no duplicate. Your three reproductions all give one copy now: 110x40 setup question with an 82-character answer narrowed to 76; the 120x24 → 76x34 corner drag; and the twelve-step narrowing drag.

I also took the over-count: `rows` is now `total == 0 ? 1 : (total - 1) / oldmsgw + 1`, so a line that fills its last row exactly no longer claims an extra row and rubs out live history above the stump. Checked with a 72-character answer at a 82-column message window shrinking to 74 — one copy, briefing still on screen.

**2 (no test types an answer and then shrinks).** That gap is why this survived six rounds, and it is now covered: a new `shrink typing` section types an answer long enough to wrap at the narrower width, narrows 100x30 → 76x30, and asserts exactly one prompt, the whole answer still present, and the conversation still on screen. Ten assertions now fail against a pre-fix binary.

Worth recording: my first version of that test asserted the prompt and answer as one joined string and failed against a *correct* build. The message window starts at column one, so joining the wrapped rows puts the left margin in the middle of the answer. It counts the characters instead now, with a comment saying why.

**3 (`\r` in `note_out`).** Fixed — a carriage return ends the line as a newline does, with your `pause()` reasoning in the comment.

**4 (`cursor_at_prompt` reset).** Now cleared in the `KEY_RESIZE` branch immediately before the repaint, so the invariant is local and does not depend on `sync_size` having taken its resized path.

**5 (`want`'s 160).** Commented, naming `readinput()`'s 128-byte callers and the 126 the reader can fill — and, in the same note, why `onscreen` and `row_blank`'s row are deliberately narrower than a wide terminal, with the invariant that makes that safe and the condition that would break it.

`ctest` is rerunning in both build types; `tui.sh` is green and `shellcheck -s sh` clean.

A resize was noticed and then sat on. The panels were rebuilt at the
next prompt, so dragging the window while the game waited on "hit space
bar to continue" left them the old size with the new columns empty
beside them, for as long as the player took to press a key -- a game
that looked like it had stopped. Typing was worse: wgetnstr returned
ERR on the resize and threw the half-typed answer away with it, so the
prompt looked untouched and the game got only whatever was typed after.

tui_getch can repaint where the old comment said it could not: curses
reports the resize by returning from wgetch, so nothing is reading the
screen at that moment. The line reader now works the same way, a
keystroke at a time instead of wgetnstr, which is what lets a resize be
handled between them -- and it keeps its own buffer, so nothing is lost.
Ctrl-D ends the session on its own keystroke now rather than needing an
Enter after it, backspace steps back a row on a wrapped answer, and
Ctrl-U clears the line, which wgetnstr did for us before.

The hard half is that curses clips the message window when it processes
the resize, and it does that before handing the game KEY_RESIZE. By the
time the game is told, the bottom rows are gone -- and on a shrink those
rows are the prompt and the answer. Two attempts at scrolling ahead of
it failed for the same reason: the clip has already happened. So the
game keeps the line it is part way through writing, and puts it back
when it went. Where the terminal only grew nothing can have been
clipped and none of this runs; where it lost columns the stump's height
is arithmetic from the old width, and those rows are rubbed out and
rewritten in place, anchored to the last row with anything on it rather
than to the bottom of the window -- the setup conversation and anything
after a clearscreen sit mid-window, where a bottom anchor left a stump
stranded above.

typed over it, a search that matched an older prompt and parked the
cursor in the history, and copies that stacked one per step of a drag.

the build before this one.

shrink-while-typing case typed at the command prompt, where the window
is already full, so bottom-anchored and line-anchored are the same row
and a reverted fix passed. The setup question is where they differ, and
that is what the second case does.

content.text:
#46 is closed — merged as `66c8ca6`, all four CI legs green including both macOS pty runs, branch deleted, tree clean.

**What it does now.** Resize the terminal at any point and the display follows immediately — during a pause, mid-answer, growing or shrinking — and both the question and the half-typed answer survive. Ctrl-D ends the session on its own keystroke, backspace works across a wrapped answer, Ctrl-U clears the line.

**The finding that shaped the whole thing:** ncurses clips the message window when *it* processes the resize, before the game is ever told. By the time `KEY_RESIZE` arrives the prompt is already gone. Two of my fixes failed for exactly that reason before I instrumented a build and saw `getmaxy(wmsg)` already reading the new size. That's why the game now keeps the line it's writing and puts it back, rather than trying to preserve what's on screen.

**This was the most expensive thing in the session, and honestly so.** Six review rounds found six distinct defects in the hand-rolled reader — a doubled echo that made the screen disagree with the buffer, duplicated setup questions, a line chopped mid-word, a cursor left in front of the answer, a search matching an older prompt and parking the cursor in the command history, and copies stacking one per drag step. Each was real and player-visible; none would have been caught by the tests I'd written at the time.

The seventh finding is the one I'd single out: `code-review` tested *my test* by building a reverted-anchor binary, and the suite still passed. My shrink-while-typing case typed at the command prompt, where the window is already full — so the two anchorings compute the same row and a reverted fix sails through. The setup conversation is where they differ. That's the rule from `0a075a5` applied to me by someone else, and it's the fifth vacuous assertion this session.

Eleven assertions now fail against the pre-fix build. Plain mode and the golden recordings are byte-identical; 29 `tui` runs under load found no flakes; ASan/UBSan clean.

**Two things I deliberately did not fix**, both reproducing on `main`: the layout below 72x24 (**#78**, filed) and a stray glyph in the message window's unowned right-hand column — `ui-review` initially attributed that to me, then retracted after reproducing it on `main`.

The tracker now has no issues about the game itself. All six remaining are process integrity: **#65, #66, #71, #72** from the workflow work, plus **#76** (assert the score columns from the compiled game) and **#78**.
